findings.reason: a worker who runs the shipped configuration gets live_pp=0 and cannot construct the generating state at all, so the section is unsatisfiable and §7, which waits on it, never starts; stating the basis as a shared precondition of the run (as the section already does for the disabled priors) is what makes the endpoint reachable.
findings.text: §8 makes the generating state's profiles "members of the basis imas-efit resolves for this run", but that basis is not a fact the worker chooses: configuration/machines/ITER/efitOptions.xml inherits the shared template's autoDegree, and src/timeSliceNumericalControls.cpp:applyAutoDegree initialises ppDeg=0 and only elevates a family that the regime row already raised, so a magnetics-only ITER slice resolves live_pp=0 (recorded AUTODEGREE line: regime=magnetics-only/large-aspect pp_ndeg=0 ff_ndeg=2 live_pp=0 live_ff=1), while the plan's own §2 comment states ITER's resolved fit as "one live p′ and two live FF′ functions" — the basis a magnetics-only nova-configured run yields therefore contains only p′≡0, which the delivered §8 run measured as raising NoQualifiedAxisError (job 1321000) and which the run only escaped by adding its own configuration naming both degrees — so §8 as written asks for a generating state in a basis that, under the configuration the section describes (priors disabled), admits no qualified state, and its clause (1) demands convergence and bands with no branch for that outcome

findings.reason: a band that an arbitrary gauge constant satisfies cannot fail, so the node's flux check reduces to the span while the plan claims five bands; moving the band onto the flux span and reporting the gauge constant makes the band able to fail and makes it match the record it cites.
findings.text: §8 clause (2) requires "the boundary and axis flux within 2 % of the axis-to-boundary span after each state's stored flux sign is read and one additive constant, reported in the record, aligns the two maps' axis flux"; once an additive constant is chosen to align the two axis fluxes the axis-flux difference is zero by construction, so that half of the band holds for any reconstruction however wrong, and only the flux span carries information — the delivered §8 record shows what the informative measure looks like (axis flux −73.211 Wb against −73.528 Wb, span 76.366 Wb, a 0.317 Wb difference reported as 0.41 % of the span, with the +0.3 Wb constant used only for the overlay figure), so the clause as written describes a measurement that cannot fail, not the one the record delivers
